references.text: The preceding verse describes how the Levite's concubine was found lying at the door in the morning, providing context for his command to get up.
Abraham loaded wood on the donkey before going to Mount Moriah, a parallel to how the Levite placed his dead concubine on the donkey to travel home.
The Levite later told the tribes of Israel what had happened to his concubine and how he brought her back home.
Abigail rode on a donkey when she met David, an example of how donkeys were used as a means of transport in similar situations.
The prophet picked up the dead man and placed him on a donkey to bring him back, a parallel action to the Levite's transport of his dead concubine.
